# BorderedElementOptions

<!-- Generated from the doc comments in the library. Do not edit this file. -->

Options for elements with borders and backgrounds (`Container`, `Table`, `TableCell`). Intersects [`ElementOptions`](element-options.md), mirroring the real inheritance chain.

Import from `@bonniepdf/core`.

```typescript
type BorderedElementOptions = ElementOptions & Partial<Omit<Pick<BorderedElementBase, BorderedOwnKey>, BorderedWidenedKey>> & {
    /**
     * Border widths, and optionally their colour.
     *
     * Accepts a uniform width, a per-side object, or `{ width, color }`.
     * Omitted sides are zero.
     *
     * BonniePDF models widths and colours as separate properties (`border` +
     * `borderColors`), so the colour-carrying form resolves to both. The
     * `border` **property setter** deliberately never writes `borderColors` - a
     * setter must not mutate a sibling - which is why this sugar lives here, in
     * the options layer, and is applied by
     * {@link applyBorderedElementOptions}.
     */
    border?: BorderInput;
    /** Background fill. Accepts a palette token (`'slate-100'`) or hex. */
    backgroundColor?: ColorInput;
    /** Corner radius. Accepts a length: `6`, `'2mm'`, or `{ value, unit }`. */
    cornerRadius?: LengthInput;
}
```

## Properties

- [`backgroundColor`](#backgroundcolor): Background fill.
- [`border`](#border): Border widths, and optionally their colour.
- [`borderColors`](#bordercolors): Border colors for each side of the element
- [`breakAllowed`](#breakallowed): Whether this element can be split across page boundaries.
- [`captureName`](#capturename): Optional author-supplied name/key surfaced in the layout snapshot.
- [`contentDirection`](#contentdirection): Inline progression and paragraph base direction; omitted inherits.
- [`cornerRadius`](#cornerradius): Corner radius.
- [`keepWithNext`](#keepwithnext): Keeps this element with the start of its next sibling in vertical flow.
- [`margin`](#margin): Margin around this element.

### `backgroundColor`

```typescript
backgroundColor?: ColorInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Background fill. Accepts a palette token (`'slate-100'`) or hex.

### `border`

```typescript
border?: BorderInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Border widths, and optionally their colour.

Accepts a uniform width, a per-side object, or `{ width, color }`. Omitted sides are zero.

BonniePDF models widths and colours as separate properties (`border` + `borderColors`), so the colour-carrying form resolves to both. The `border` **property setter** deliberately never writes `borderColors` - a setter must not mutate a sibling - which is why this sugar lives here, in the options layer, and is applied by `applyBorderedElementOptions`.

### `borderColors`

```typescript
borderColors?: BorderColors | undefined
```

*optional*

Border colors for each side of the element

### `breakAllowed`

```typescript
breakAllowed?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Whether this element can be split across page boundaries. When false, the element is treated as atomic and will be moved to a new page rather than split. If it doesn't fit on a fresh page either, it renders anyway. Default is true.

### `captureName`

```typescript
captureName?: string | undefined
```

*optional*

Optional author-supplied name/key surfaced in the layout snapshot. Unset by default; a future capture API can populate it.

### `contentDirection`

```typescript
contentDirection?: ContentDirectionInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Inline progression and paragraph base direction; omitted inherits.

### `cornerRadius`

```typescript
cornerRadius?: LengthInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Corner radius. Accepts a length: `6`, `'2mm'`, or `{ value, unit }`.

### `keepWithNext`

```typescript
keepWithNext?: boolean | undefined
```

*optional*

Keeps this element with the start of its next sibling in vertical flow.

### `margin`

```typescript
margin?: ThicknessInput | undefined
```

*optional*

Margin around this element. Accepts `12`, `[h, v]`, `[l, t, r, b]` or `{ bottom: 12 }`; omitted sides are zero.
